releases.label: Launchers
releases.title: Launchers for Windows and Steam Deck
releases.summary: Frontface now installs and updates through its own launcher on Windows and on the Steam Deck, with builds from GitHub. The browser version went live the same day, and servers can take browser players.

entries.title: Frontface Launcher.
entries.text: Install, update and play Windows builds, keep older versions side by side, join a server by its address, and read these notes.

entries.title: Steam Deck launcher.
entries.text: A Linux launcher for the Deck that works with the controller in Game Mode, opens Steam's keyboard for the Join box, and updates itself.

entries.title: Native Linux build.
entries.text: From 0.1.1 every version also comes for Linux, so the Deck runs Frontface without Proton. Windows and Deck players can join each other's servers.

entries.title: Play in the browser.
entries.text: frontface-neon.vercel.app runs the game against bots in Chrome with WebGPU, no install.

entries.title: Servers for browser players.
entries.text: A dedicated server can speak WebSockets (websocket = 1 in server.cfg), so browser and desktop players can play on the same server.

entries.title: Controller support.
entries.text: Move, aim, lean while aiming, throw gadgets and work the menus with a gamepad.

entries.title: Steady aim.
entries.text: Hold sprint while scoped to hold your breath against the sway.

entries.title: Stims for every class.
entries.text: Every class can carry a stim shot.

entries.title: 12 more guns.
entries.text: More guns for every class.

entries.title: Every launcher for Support.
entries.text: Support can now carry all of the launchers.

entries.title: Display and Resolution settings.
entries.text: Choose full screen or windowed and a resolution under Settings, Graphics.

entries.title: Black bars under Proton.
entries.text: Full screen at the wrong shape snaps back to the monitor's size, and the Resolution list uses that real size (0.1.1 and 0.1.2).

releases.label: Arsenal
releases.title: Thirty-three guns, launchers and a dedicated server
releases.summary: Every gun rebuilt from real photographs, a gun list per class, launchers, new ways to move, new maps and a server you can run at home.

entries.title: 33 guns, each owned by a class.
entries.text: Assault, Support, Medic, Recon and Breacher each have their own guns; pistols go with any class. Lengths are within a few millimetres of the real ones.

entries.title: Launchers.
entries.text: LAW, Carl Gustaf, RPG-7 and M32, plus M203 and GP-25 grenade launchers under the rifle.

entries.title: Two gadget slots and killstreaks.
entries.text: Each class picks two gadgets, and a run of kills earns more.

entries.title: Optics that really magnify.
entries.text: A 4x scope shows 4x, measured on a target at 60 m. Canted sights for close range.

entries.title: New ways to move.
entries.text: Prone, dive to prone, crouch slide, vault over cover and through windows, mount your gun on cover while aiming, and a tactical sprint (double-tap Shift).

entries.title: Redwing Airfield and Old Town.
entries.text: Two new maps, and The Depot redone as a mirrored map so neither side starts ahead.

entries.title: Dedicated server.
entries.text: A Windows server package with server.cfg and a map rotation that keeps players between matches.

entries.title: A voice for every soldier.
entries.text: Each soldier keeps one voice for all of their lines.

entries.title: Guns rebuilt.
entries.text: Low poly but detailed: real cuts, rounded grips, pins, knurling and roll marks, with smoother reloads.

entries.title: Hands sit on the gun.
entries.text: Both hands reach the grip, handguard and charging handle in first and third person, through every reload.

entries.title: Smoke, fire and light.
entries.text: Soft lit smoke, flame, light shafts and indoor exposure.

entries.title: Graphics options.
entries.text: Anti-aliasing, shadows, ambient occlusion, depth of field, bloom, motion blur, grain, light shafts, render scale and a frame cap.

entries.title: Bots.
entries.text: Bots notice you gradually and fight at the range their gun suits.

entries.title: Shots stopped by invisible walls.
entries.text: Bullets now hit the shape of the cover you see, not a box around it.

releases.label: First playable
releases.title: Frontface is playable
releases.summary: Conquest against bots or friends, real guns with real reloads, your own classes and four maps.

entries.title: Conquest.
entries.text: Take and hold the flags; the side that runs out of tickets loses.

entries.title: Six real guns.
entries.text: M4A1, AK-74, MP5A3, Glock 17, Model 870 and M24, with magazine reloads and spent brass.

entries.title: Online play.
entries.text: Host a game or join one by address.

entries.title: Create a class.
entries.text: Five saved classes, attachments for every gun, and gadgets for each role.

entries.title: Four maps.
entries.text: The Depot, Sandstone, Port Anvil and Timberline.

images.alt: A watchtower among pines on Timberline
images.caption: Timberline

entries.title: The interface.
entries.text: Title screen, loading, deploy, pause, settings, death and end-of-match screens.

entries.title: Props from the 3D studio.
entries.text: Seventeen props, from the APC to the satellite dish, made in the AI 3D studio and drawn in the game's own style.

inProgress.title: A real Steam Deck
inProgress.body: The Deck launcher and the Linux build were tested on Linux on a PC: installing, and joining a server from the launcher. Running them on a Deck, with the game drawn on the Deck's own GPU, comes next.

inProgress.title: A public server
inProgress.body: Servers work on a home PC. Browser players also need a secure (wss://) address, and the way to provide one hasn't been chosen yet.

inProgress.title: Real controllers
inProgress.body: Controller support was built and tested with scripted input; it still needs a real gamepad in hand.

inProgress.title: Playing by hand
inProgress.body: Every build is checked by scripts. Long matches with a real mouse, LAN games and listening to the new sounds come next.
